title: Adjectives of the First and Second Declension
subtitle: ἀγαθός, ἀγαθή, ἀγαθόν — agreement and position.
objectives: Decline any first- and second-declension adjective in all three genders.
Understand that adjectives agree with nouns in gender, number, and case.
Distinguish attributive position from predicate position.
Translate adjectives in both positions correctly.

sections.heading: Adjectives
sections.body:
Greek adjectives decline like nouns. A first- and second-declension adjective has three forms: masculine (second declension), feminine (first declension), neuter (second declension). The adjective agrees with the noun it modifies in gender, number, and case.

ἀγαθός, ἀγαθή, ἀγαθόν (good) is the model adjective. The masculine follows the second declension like λόγος. The feminine follows the first declension like ἀρετή. The neuter follows the second declension like δῶρον.

sections.heading: The paradigm: ἀγαθός, ἀγαθή, ἀγαθόν
sections.body:
Masculine (second declension):
              singular        plural
  nominative  ἀγαθός          ἀγαθοί
  genitive    ἀγαθοῦ          ἀγαθῶν
  dative      ἀγαθῷ           ἀγαθοῖς
  accusative  ἀγαθόν          ἀγαθούς
  vocative    ἀγαθέ           ἀγαθοί

Feminine (first declension):
              singular        plural
  nominative  ἀγαθή           ἀγαθαί
  genitive    ἀγαθῆς          ἀγαθῶν
  dative      ἀγαθῇ           ἀγαθαῖς
  accusative  ἀγαθήν          ἀγαθάς
  vocative    ἀγαθή           ἀγαθαί

Neuter (second declension):
              singular        plural
  nominative  ἀγαθόν          ἀγαθά
  genitive    ἀγαθοῦ          ἀγαθῶν
  dative      ἀγαθῷ           ἀγαθοῖς
  accusative  ἀγαθόν          ἀγαθά
  vocative    ἀγαθόν          ἀγαθά

sections.heading: Attributive and predicate position
sections.body:
Adjectives can be used in two ways.

Attributive position: the adjective is inside the article-noun phrase. ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος or ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἀγαθός — 'the good man'. The adjective modifies the noun.

Predicate position: the adjective is outside the article-noun phrase. ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἀγαθός or ἀγαθὸς ὁ ἄνθρωπος — 'the man is good'. The adjective is the predicate, and a form of εἰμί is implied or stated.

This distinction is signaled by position, not by word order. ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος and ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἀγαθός both mean 'the good man' (attributive). ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἀγαθός and ἀγαθὸς ὁ ἄνθρωπος both mean 'the man is good' (predicate).

sections.heading: Examples from Plato
sections.body:
Plato, Republic 331c: ὁ δίκαιος ἀνήρ.
'The just man.' Attributive position.

Plato, Republic 335e: ὁ ἀνὴρ ἀγαθός ἐστιν.
'The man is good.' Predicate position with an explicit εἰμί.

sections.heading: Self-check
sections.instructions: Cover the answers. Parse or translate.

items.answer: The adjective is inside the article-noun phrase.
The adjective is outside the article-noun phrase.
Yes — in gender, number, and case.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can decline ἀγαθός, ἀγαθή, ἀγαθόν from memory and can correctly identify and translate ten sentences with adjectives in attributive and predicate position.
